questions.q: What did the Israelites do after celebrating the Festival of the Unleavened Bread?
questions.a: The people of Israel went out to the cities of Judah, broke the sacred stone pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, broke down the shrines and altars in Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all.

questions.q: Where did the people of Israel go after they did this?
questions.a: They returned to their own land and city.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah assign the priests and the Levites to do after he organized them by their divisions?
questions.a: Hezekiah assigned them to make burnt offerings, fellowship offerings, to serve, to give thanks, and to praise at the gates of Yahweh’s temple.

questions.q: What portion did Hezekiah assign and when was it to be offered?
questions.a: The portion was to be a king’s portion from his own possessions, and the burnt offerings were for the morning, evening, Sabbath days, the new moons, and the fixed festivals.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah command the people of Jerusalem to do so the priests and Levites might concentrate on obeying the law of Yahweh?
questions.a: The people were to give a portion for the priests and Levites.

questions.q: What happened when the command went out to the people?
questions.a: The people of Israel gave the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and from the harvest of the field to all in abundance. They also gave the tithe of all things.

questions.q: What did the people in the cities of Judah do about the command?
questions.a: The people in the cities of Judah brought the tithe of oxen, sheep, and a tithe of things that were consecrated to Yahweh, laying them in heaps.

questions.q: What were the months when the people laid the heaps?
questions.a: The people laid the heaps beginning in the third month and finishing the heaps in the seventh month.

questions.q: Who blessed Yahweh and the people when they saw the heaps?
questions.a: Hezekiah and the leaders blessed Yahweh and the people.

questions.q: How did Azariah, the chief priest, answer Hezekiah when he asked the priests and the Levites about the heaps?
questions.a: Azariah answered that the people brought the tithes and put them in these large heaps. He told Hezekiah that they had eaten enough, and these heaps were left over because Yahweh had blessed the people.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah command to be prepared and what did the people do?
questions.a: Hezekiah commanded storerooms be prepared in the house of Yahweh. Then the people prepared them and brought in the offerings, tithes, and consecrated things.

questions.q: Who did Hezekiah and Azariah appoint to be managers in charge of the storerooms?
questions.a: Hezekiah and Azariah appointed Conaniah manager in charge with Conaniah’s brother, Shimei, as manager second in charge.

questions.q: To whom did Kore and those with him distribute the offerings?
questions.a: They distributed to those males three years old and up, division by division, who were counted in the genealogies that entered the house of Yahweh that did the work in their positions.

questions.q: Who was counted next to receive the offerings?
questions.a: They gave to the Levites twenty years old and up that were filling their positions division by division.

questions.q: What had the people done before receiving the offerings from Kore and those with him?
questions.a: The people had consecrated themselves before the distribution to all their little ones, their wives, and their sons and daughters, who were counted in their genealogies.

questions.q: What was done for the priests who were counted in the genealogies as being among the Levites?
questions.a: There were men assigned to give portions to all the males who were in the fields of the villages that belonged to the cities or in every city.

questions.q: Where did Hezekiah accomplish this and how was it done?
questions.a: Hezekiah accomplished this throughout all Judah and it was done good, right, and faithful before Yahweh.

questions.q: In what way did Hezekiah perform each project, and what was the result?
questions.a: Hezekiah performed all these projects with all his heart, and he succeeded.

commentary.text: —After the passover, the people of Israel applied with vigour to destroy the monuments of idolatry. Public ordinances should stir us up to cleanse our hearts, our houses, and shops, from the filth of sin, and the idolatry of covetousness, and to excite others to do the same. The after-improvement of solemn ordinances, is of the greatest importance to personal, family, and public religion. When they had tasted the sweetness of God's ordinance in the late passover, they were free in maintaining the temple service. Those who enjoy the benefit of a settled ministry, will not grudge the expense of it. In all that Hezekiah attempted in God's service, he was earnest and single in his aim and dependence, and was prospered accordingly. Whether we have few or many talents intrusted to us, may we thus seek to improve them, and encourage others to do the same. What is undertaken with a sincere regard to the glory of God, will succeed to our own honour and comfort at last.
